Mortimer rushes to tell Abby and Martha before they stumble upon the body themselves, only to learn that the two women aren t just aware of the dead man in their parlor, they killed him! title: Auburn Symphony Orchestra: Rhythm & Revelry
description: NULL
big_desc: A season finale is a celebration. Rhythm & Revelry begins with sacred joy in Omar Thomas Come Sunday, a tribute to the Hammond organ s central place in Black worship. The first movement, Testimony, prepares the spirit with a sound world shaped by Bach, blues, jazz, and R&B. The second, Shout!, bursts into the ecstatic moment when celebration takes over. Thomas writes with love, energy, and purpose, honoring Black culture through music that sings, moves, and lifts the room. From there, the spotlight turns to violinist Nathan Amaral in Tchaikovsky s Violin Concerto. Born in Rio de Janeiro, Amaral began violin through a social project in Mangueira and has since become one of the most compelling young violinists on the international stage. He won First Prize at the 2024 Sphinx Competition and the Grand Prize of the 2024 CAG-YCAT Competitions, and Yo-Yo Ma has praised his rare ability to move beyond technique into the heart of musical expression. Tchaikovsky s concerto gives him a perfect canvas: soaring melodies, dazzling passagework, and emotional sweep from first note to last. Then Auburn Symphony takes center stage. Ravel s Boléro begins with a single rhythm and one unforgettable theme, repeating again and again as the music grows from a whisper to a blaze. Each section of the orchestra gets its moment to shine, turning one simple idea into a thrilling display of color and control. Strauss Der Rosenkavalier Suite brings the afternoon to a lavish close. Drawn from his beloved opera, the suite mixes romantic sweep with elegant waltzes and the glittering richness of Vienna imagined through Strauss 20th-century orchestral voice. From worship to virtuosity to full-orchestra spectacle, Rhythm & Revelry sends the season out with brilliance, abundance, and joy.

title: Auburn Symphony Orchestra: Symphonic Stories
description: NULL
big_desc: Some forces are invisible, but you feel their pull. Symphonic Stories brings together three works about distance, memory, imagination, and the stories that hold us together. A voice reaches across grief. A soloist moves through shifting celestial worlds. A woman tells story after story, surviving one night at a time. Jennifer Higdon s blue cathedral begins the journey in a place of remembrance. Written after the death of her brother, Andrew Blue Higdon, the piece imagines a vast sacred space filled with light, crystal, and upward motion. The flute, Higdon s instrument, and the clarinet, her brother s instrument, move through the music like two voices reaching toward one another. It is a work of loss, but also of release: a quiet ascent through memory toward something larger. From there, Auburn Symphony looks outward with the Co-Commission of Gravity at a Distance, a new saxophone concerto by Viet Cuong written for Timothy McAllister. The concerto takes inspiration from celestial bodies and the unseen forces that bind them across immense distances. The solo saxophone moves through orchestral worlds that feel luminous, floating, dense, and immense, tracing a path between isolation and attraction, stillness and motion. Then comes one of music s great storytellers. Rimsky-Korsakov s Scheherazade draws from One Thousand and One Nights, where Scheherazade survives a violent ruler not through force, but through intelligence, wit, and imagination. Each night, she tells a story compelling enough to earn another dawn. In the orchestra, her voice returns through the solo violin: persuasive, resilient, and unbroken. With blue cathedral, Gravity at a Distance, and Scheherazade, Symphonic Stories becomes a concert about what connects us across silence, space, and danger. These are stories of remembrance, invention, and survival, told in the language of the orchestra.

title: Auburn Symphony Orchestra: The Music of Studio Ghibli

A young girl wanders into a bathhouse for gods. A castle lumbers across the hills on impossible legs. For generations of fans, Studio Ghibli has created animated films that feel both fantastical and deeply human. Founded in Japan and closely associated with filmmaker Hayao Miyazaki, the studio has become one of the most beloved names in animation, with stories known for wonder, adventure, environmental beauty, and characters who find courage in unfamiliar worlds. At the heart of many of those films is the music of Joe Hisaishi. His scores do more than accompany the action. They give these worlds their breath, motion, and emotional pull. Like John Williams long partnership with Steven Spielberg, Hisaishi s music has helped shape the identity of the films themselves. Led by Music Director Wesley Schulz, Auburn Symphony celebrates the music of Kiki s Delivery Service, My Neighbor Totoro, Spirited Away, and Howl s Moving Castle in a concert filled with soaring melodies, playful characters, sweeping orchestral color, and moments of quiet beauty. Fans will recognize the themes they love. New listeners will hear why this music has reached far beyond the screen. The Music of Studio Ghibli is a concert for families, anime fans, film lovers, and anyone ready for an evening of adventure, nostalgia, and imagination.

big_desc:
As the days grow shorter, heading outdoors can feel harder. But gathering with others in the daylight among the trees and the water is a grounding practice that can help us live through the cooler season with intention. Take a break from life s pressures and join us for this late fall walk at the beautiful Wapato Park. We will listen to the trees, pay attention to the many native plants around us, breathe in together and reflect by the lake.

Make sure to check the forecast. Bring layers, comfortable shoes, water, and anything else you need to be comfortable. We hold our walks rain or shine. If in doubt, please check our social media and website calendar for updates.

This walk will be offered in Spanish and English thanks to our partner Claudia Linares from Girasol Counseling.

Cuando los días se hacen más cortos, se nos antoja menos salir de casa. Pero reunirnos con otra gente en el día, entre los árboles y cerca del agua, puede revitalizarnos en la temporada de frío y ayudarnos a vivir el invierno con más intención. Te invitamos a descansar de las presiones del día a día en esta caminata otoñal en el hermoso Wapato Park. Pondremos atención a lo que nos dicen los árboles y las plantas autóctonas que nos rodean. Respiraremos hondo y reflexionaremos juntes a la orilla del lago.

Consulta el clima antes de salir de casa. Te recomendamos usar capas, zapatos cómodos, y traer cualquier otra cosa que sea necesaria para que estés cómode durante nuestro tiempo juntos. Sólo cancelamos nuestras caminatas si el clima supone un riesgo para los asistentes. Si tienes dudas, consulta nuestro sitio web y medios sociales para confirmar el estatus del evento.

Esta caminata es una colaboración entre TTF, Strategic Nature, y Girasol Counseling.

Federales music has appeared in films, including A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night , The Bad Batch , and The Lego Movie , while the band has toured extensively throughout North America and Europe. Federales newest album Love & Other Lies (2026) teems with a dark sentimentality and a pronounced gloomy sensibility drawing from British new wave, post-punk, goth, and 1960s rock n roll. Strains of The Cure, Depeche Mode, The Sisters of Mercy, Siouxsie and the Banshees, Tears for Fears, and even The Beatles abound. Here, lead singer and primary songwriter Collin Hegnas emotive baritone is swathed in period-perfect Prophet-5 synthesizers and glistening counter-melody guitar lines, and supported by intricate but lyrical basslines and coldly mechanical drums. Love & Other Lies picks up where Federales previous album, Reverb & Seduction , left off. That album was a radical departure from the bands previous releases which featured mostly instrumentals. There are a lot more similarities than you think, Hegna says of the groups seemingly two distinct aesthetic periods. When we were referencing the obscure influences, we liked the drama and darkness. Those elements are in new wave, goth, and post-punk. I just grabbed another couple of colors from the Crayon box. Together they make (mostly) wordless sound eruptions that have only best been described as if Danny Elfman and Eliot Smith had a baby and if fell down a spiral staircase in New Orleans Come try and describe the ear twisting music yourself! big_desc:
Lecture 6 | Dale Chihuly

How Tacoma s own Chihuly brought Studio Glass into the global imagination, inspiring countless artists and redefining glass as large-scale public art.

In celebration of America s 250th anniversary in 2026, and in partnership with America 250, Forged in Fire at Museum of Glass will combine illustrated lectures, live glassblowing demonstrations, and multimedia content to trace the evolution of American glassmaking, from colonial Jamestown to the contemporary works of Dale Chihuly. Each event illuminates the artistry, design, and cultural significance of glass as both a decorative and functional medium. Forged in Fire will reach diverse audiences throughout the Puget Sound region and beyond via in-person events and live streams, and build community pride in the region s unique role in the American Studio Glass Movement — a movement co-founded by Tacoma-native Dale Chihuly. By combining history, artistry, and live craft, this program exemplifies how decorative arts can spark curiosity, fuel discovery, and create shared cultural experiences.

Lectures and Demonstrations

Museum of Glass will host six unique public sessions pairing glass history talks by renowned glass artist and historian Walter Lieberman with live demonstrations by the Museum s internationally acclaimed Hot Shop Team. Each lecture focuses on a specific period of time in glassmaking history and is accompanied by a demonstration that recreates period-specific objects and techniques, giving audiences tangible insight into the evolution of glass as a decorative art form. All lectures will take place on select Saturdays 1pm in the Museum of Glass Hot Shop. The glassmaking demonstrations will follow at 2pm.

The live show, which has been called hilarious and fascinating by Time Out New York, combines hypnosis and improv for a one-of-a-kind comedy experience. We are so excited to launch this new tour and return to some of our favorite cities and visit some new ones, said Asad Mecci. It s been an incredible journey. And we just want to remind everyone, YES! It s real, exclaims Colin Mochrie. HYPROV has been acclaimed by prestigious publications, with The New York Times declaring, The audience erupted in laughter. It killed. The Wall Street Journal praised it as catnip for those who relish spontaneity and informality, and The New Yorker advised, Say yes to HYPROV. The 90-minute show combines hypnosis and improv—two art forms that have mystified and entertained fans, skeptics, and everyone in between. The evening begins with Mecci welcoming 20 volunteers on stage to be hypnotized. The most receptive to hypnosis then join Mochrie to improvise the rest of the show while hypnotized. In the hands of two experts and solely crafted from the volunteers and audiences uninhibited, unconscious minds, each show is an entirely original and completely unforgettable theatrical experience. HYPROV was created in 2016 at Toronto s Second City. After working it out on stage, they took the show on the road to Just for Laughs London, Just for Laughs Montreal, and the Edinburgh Fringe, where it was received with rave reviews in 2016 and 2017. The duo set out on a 100-city tour from 2019 to 2023, performed 12 weeks off-Broadway in NYC, six months at Harrah s Las Vegas, and a 16-show residency at the CAA Theatre in Toronto. Come enjoy an intimate evening of world class jazz in Tacomas own exclusive downtown Speakeasy.

Guests are invited to bring their own food and drinks to the performance.

Kareem Kandi - saxophone

Paul Gabrielson - bass

Ali Jackson- drums

The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra is a dynamic and innovative ensemble committed to providing high-quality performances and music education to communities worldwide. Through a blend of concerts, workshops, compositions, recordings, and cultural exchanges, the orchestra brings people together through the universal language of music, with a special emphasis on the rich traditions of jazz.

Led by saxophonist, composer, and educator Kareem Kandi, the orchestra draws on his vast experience as a performer who has earned acclaim for his work in jazz, blues, classical, and funk. A native of the Pacific Northwest, Kareems versatility as a saxophonist and composer has taken him across the U.S. and around the globe, captivating audiences and critics alike. Known for his ability to honor the traditions of the past while forging new creative pathways, Kareems compositions and unique arrangements of timeless American standards continue to push musical boundaries.

Since 1996, Kareem has performed as both a bandleader and sideman, sharing the stage with luminaries such as Patti Labelle, Ali Jackson, George Colligan, Pete Christlieb, Bill Watrous, The Seattle Symphony, The Paperboys, The Temptations, The Four Tops, and many more. His work with The Kareem Kandi World Orchestra featuring embodies a sound that is fresh, innovative, and appeals to a diverse range of audiences. Each member brings decades of experience and mastery of their instruments, contributing to a performance that transcends genres and connects with listeners on many levels.

About Ali Jackson:

Ali Jackson has performed and recorded with a multitude of artists including Wynton Marsalis, Jon Batiste, Willie Nelson, Tony Bennett, Faith Hill, Karriem Riggins, Bobby McFerrin, Buster Williams, Norah Jones, Eric Clapton, Dee Dee Bridgewater, Aretha Franklin, George Benson, Harry Connick, Jr., KRS-1, Marcus Roberts, Joshua Redman, Vinx, Seito Kinen, Seiji Ozawa, Diana Krall, Gerald Albright, Michael Heise, Russell Gunn, James Morrison, Craig Handy, Jacky Terrasson, Kurt Rosenwinkel, and the New York City Ballet.

As a bandleader, Ali has recorded five albums, including Amalgamations, Wheelz Keep Rollin , Big Brown Getdown and the Yes! Trio album. Ali s playing is featured on more than 40 other albums, including Congo Square, Touchdown, Gunn Fu, Young Gunn Plus, European Sessions, Live at Yoshi s, Reflections in Change, Back East, Two Men With The Blues, Three-Five, Here We Go Again: Celebrating the Genius of Ray Charles, He and She, The Magic Hour and From the Plantation to the Penitentiary. Jackson also collaborated with jazz greats Cyrus Chestnut, Reginald Veal, and James

Carter on Gold Sounds, an innovative album that sought to transform songs by indie alternative rock band Pavement into unique virtuosic interpretations with the spirit of the church and the attitude of the juke joint. His production skills can be heard on George Benson s album Irreplaceable. He is also the voice of Duck Ellington, a character in the Penguin book series Baby Loves Jazz.

Ali is also an acclaimed composer whose voice is unique in its command of the universal language of the groove and the power of thoughtful use of space — both rhythmically and harmonically. His most recent masterworks include the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra-commissioned Living Grooves: A World in Jazz Rhythm and a ballet composed for the Alvin Ailey Dance Company titled r-Evolution, Dream.

Ali s collaborations with other artists continue to push the envelope of jazz music and its connection to the human spirit. In 2010, Ali executive produced an original work called Beats of NYC, a project blending the musical idioms of Congolese, Senegalese, Tap, and modern dances juxtaposed with various styles of spoken word and the history of the blues. He also composed a ballet with long-time collaborator Hope Boykin titled Ballet: Watching go by the Day.

Junior Community Scientists

Ever wondered what it s like to participate in community science projects? Join Communities for a Healthy Bay for a hands-on half-day adventure exploring Commencement Bay from the water and the shore!

Youth will depart from the CHB office aboard our boat for a bay patrol, stopping along the way to conduct real water quality testing and help record water color data for ongoing monitoring efforts. Next, they ll get up close with the bay s smallest residents during a plankton sampling session, using nets and microscopes to see what s living beneath the surface.
The adventure continues at Owen Beach, where kids will join in a Green Crab Molt Search — helping track this invasive species by combing the shoreline for shed crab shells — before refueling with a provided lunch by the water. Then it s back aboard for the cruise home to the CHB office.

Kids will leave with real hands-on science experience, a better understanding of the bay they call home, and a taste of what it means to protect it.

This program is FREE! Lunch is provided.

The resulting music will convince you that rock still has ingenuity to burn. title: Live at the Eleanor with Jazz Therapy
description: Jazz Therapy : This Christmas A Soulful Jazz Celebration – Featuring the music of This Christmas, plus soulful songs and gospel selections — Donny Hathaway, Stevie Wonder, The Carpenters, and The Preacher s Wife. THE BAND Teal Warren – Bass Pete Yankeh – Drums Henry Nielsen – Piano Bill Throssell – Trumpet & Flugel Horn Jon Fotheringill – Alto & Tenor Saxophone SPECIAL GUEST VOCALISTS Alma Villegas Cathy Satava In the vibrant tapestry of sound, where rhythm meets soul, Jazz Therapy emerges as a powerful force of musical healing. Born from the depths of rich jazz tradition and a passion for emotional expression, this dynamic ensemble brings an unparalleled fusion of soulful melodies, intricate rhythms, and exuberant improvisation that captivate audiences of all ages. Leader and visionary Teal Warren, renowned for his mastery of the bass and a deep-rooted passion for jazz as both a musician and army veteran, guides Jazz Therapy with an intuitive sense of harmony and collaboration. Drawing inspiration from many jazz legends, the ensemble creates a sonic universe where each note resonates with vibrant energy, inviting listeners to not only hear but to feel the music s transformative power. Collaborating with a talented lineup of seasoned musicians, Jazz Therapy is about more than just music—it s an experience. From the pulsing beats of slap bass to the gentle caress of a saxophone solo, every performance is a journey that fosters connection, reflection, and empowerment. This sense of unity is the bedrock of the band s philosophy, which centers on music as an innovative therapy — a sanctuary where individuals can come together, heal, and grow. With accolades that span esteemed jazz festivals and high-profile events, Jazz Therapy s eclectic repertoire seamlessly weaves in influences from modern jazz, blues, and world music, crafting a sound that s both a nod to the classics and a fresh auditory exploration. Each performance is an opportunity to not only entertain but to touch hearts and ignite spirits with the transformative magic of jazz. Jazz Therapy invites you to dive into their world, where music is the remedy and every performance is a soulful recollection of the universal language that binds us all. Whether you are a jazz connoisseur or a curious soul seeking refuge through sound, Jazz Therapy is exceptional, unforgettable, and ready to heal. Live at The Eleanor offers a cozy candlelit lounge experience where each performance unfolds like a conversation between artist and audience. Full bar and concessions are available; all ages are welcome.

Gretchen Yanover With an electric cello in hand and a loop pedal under foot, Yanover is her own one-woman band. Playing and layering her melodies, she crafts instrumental atmospheres that grow and transform onstage. – Maggie Molloy, Classic KING FM — NPR Slingshot Cellist Gretchen Yanover creates spacious string atmospheres woven with warm melodies. She performs with her electric cello and looping pedal, in addition to her acoustic cello performance and recording work. Yanover began her musical life in Seattle public schools, falling in love with the cello s deep sound. Gretchen pursued both performance and music education at University of Washington, embracing an interwoven path of teaching and performing. Ms. Yanover guided students in music for 17 years, while at the same time growing her own solo performing career. Gretchen started playing with a loop sampler around 2001 and it changed her musical life, inspiring her to improvise and compose. Yanover s 5th album will be released March 2024. Gretchen performs throughout the Pacific Northwest as a soloist on her electric cello, while continuing her classical music life. She has played with Northwest Sinfonietta orchestra since 1998, and is a member of Northwest Sinfonietta s DEI task force, working to make meaningful changes in the classical music culture, along with creating connections in the community. Northwest Sinfonietta has featured Gretchen as a soloist on her electric cello on several occasions. Yanover has appeared as a soloist for the Earshot Jazz Festival, and presented at TEDx Seattle. She created music for and performed with LeVar Burton for LeVar Burton Reads live, and has had compositions commissioned by Seattle Symphony, Seattle Pacific University, and University of Oregon. Gretchen was the recipient of a Shunpike Artist residency, and was the Town Hall Seattle 2021 Fall Artist in Residence. She is the recipient of a 2023 CityArtist grant from the Seattle Office of Arts & Culture. Gretchen loves exploring on foot, cooking vegan dishes, reading, and social tango dancing. Kick off the holiday season with a big-screen showing of Planes, Trains and Automobiles , the beloved 1987 comedy starring Steve Martin and John Candy. What starts as one man s desperate attempt to get home for Thanksgiving becomes a spectacularly chaotic cross-country journey involving canceled flights, questionable motels, rental-car disasters, and one extremely talkative shower curtain ring salesman. Come early for holiday trivia , grab your favorite movie snacks and drinks, and settle in for a Thanksgiving classic that somehow gets funnier—and a little more relatable—with age. Whether you grew up watching it on VHS, discovered it somewhere along the way, or still quote that rental car scene , consider this your official invitation to start Thanksgiving week with some laughs. No delayed flights. No awkward family dinner. Just trivia, drinks, snacks, and a holiday classic on the big screen. Planes, Trains and Automobiles is rated R. description: NULL
big_desc: Event featured image, but exclude link Event content Join us Saturday October 3rd, 1-2:30pm to hear from artist David Hytone. Project Northwest artist David Hytone will begin with a condensed history of his practice, touching on the evolution of studio techniques and visual vocabulary. Hytone will then discuss the changes in his practice that led to the creation of the Project Northwest exhibition, The Lee Shore . This free discussion will be followed by a Q&A session held in the exhibition space. This lecture is free with museum admission, but registration is encouraged. David Hytone recieved his BFA in Fines Arts from the Minneapolis College of Art and Design after studying briefly at the Osaka University of Arts in Japan. He has exhibited locally, nationally, and internationally, including shows in New York, Seattle, San Francisco, Miami, Minneapolis, Portland, Basel Switzerland, and Brussels and Ghent Belgium. A frequent visiting artist and lectuerer, David last spoke about his practice at Penn State School of Visual Arts. He has work in numerous private and corporate collections including Microsoft, Facebook, Capital One, Swedish hospitals, Hilton, SeaTac airport, and the permanent collection of King County, Washington. A 2024 MacDowell Fellow and 2018 Neddy finalist in painting currently living in Tacoma, Washington, David s next exhibition following The Lee Tide will be a solo show at Greg Kucera Gallery in April 2027. title: Project NW: Eirik Johnson Opening Reception Thursday, 6:00pm
description: NULL
big_desc: Event featured image, but exclude link Event content Eirik Johnson Madison Rose, 2023 Archival pigment print 53-1/2 x 40 inches Courtesy of Koplin Del Rio Gallery Thursday, October 29, 6–8pm Please join us to celebrate the opening of Project NW: Eirik Johnson , an exhibition featuring Leviathan Rising . From his kayak, Seattle photographic artist Eirik Johnson captures the massive hulls of trans-oceanic barges idling in the Duwamish River, exploring oceanic trade, environmental fragility, and the machinery that carries cargo through uncertain waters. The project also includes luminous, silver-plated daguerreotype photograms of Japanese fishing floats, created in collaboration with artist Daniel Carrillo. This exhibition is organized by Ellen Ito, Curator of Collections and Special Projects. The exhibition is part of Project NW , a series devoted to artists of the region. This event is free and open to the public, no registration required. Pre-order the hardcover book Leviathan Rising to take home a lasting piece of the exhibition. Eirik Johnson crafts a compelling meditation on the movement of goods, people, and histories across the Pacific, while highlighting the environmental consequences of our interconnected world. Features 68 color photographs, three gatefolds, and underwater field recordings captured in the Duwamish. Pre-order Now .tribe-events-single-event-description Event meta #post-x #tribe-events-content

The Pilgrimage by Paulo Coelho is a spiritual travel narrative inspired by Coelho s journey along the road to Santiago de Compostela in Spain. title: Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism 2026
description: The Chinese Reconciliation Project Foundation invites the public to join them and the Washington State Historical Museum at the 2026 Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism. This annual demonstration r…
big_desc:
The Chinese Reconciliation Project Foundation invites the public to join them and the Washington State Historical Museum at the 2026 Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism. This annual demonstration retraces and reverses the walking path of expulsion forced on Tacomas Chinese American population in 1885, reclaiming the City for all peoples and cultures.

The walk, led by civic, educational, business and faith leaders, will begin near Union Station, where the Chinese pioneers in 1885 were marched at gunpoint out of town. Walkers will proceed north, led by Chinese Lion Dancers, through downtown Tacoma where many Chinese, and later Japanese businesses and houses once stood, along Schuster Parkway and the railroad- largely built by Chinese labor, and finally arrive at the Chinese Reconciliation Park. Throughout the walk, attendees will be within a half mile of the Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC) where a similar white nationalist agenda continues to be orchestrated.

This year, the Opening Ceremony will take place inside the Washington State History Museums Mt. Tahoma Auditorium at 10 AM. After brief remarks from our Emcee and guest speaker, the Walk will begin from outside the Union Station around 10:45 AM. Walkers will arrive at the Chinese Reconciliation Park by 12 PM, and the event will conclude with final remarks, performances, and refreshments. To learn more about our guest speakers and our events timing, please visit our website.

Event Timing

  • Welcome Speeches begin at 10 AM, in the Washington State History Museum s Mt. Tahoma Auditorium.
  • The walk begins at 11 AM, from the History Museum s auditorium to the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park.
  • The Conclusion Ceremony begins at 12:30 PM, at the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park, featuring remarks from local dignitaries, a performance, and refreshments.

This event is free, open to all and families and children are most welcome. Join us in solidarity on Saturday, October 24th as we commit ourselves to anti-racism in the City of Destiny

Bus Schedule

To ensure our Walk for Reconciliation Against Racism is inclusive and accessible to all, we have organized a bus to transport participants who are unable to walk the three mile distance from the Union Station to the Tacoma Chinese Reconciliation Park.

  • The bus leaves the Union Station area at 10:45 AM, to transport attendees to the Chinese Reconciliation Park
  • The bus back leaves the Chinese Reconciliation Park at 1:15 PM, bringing attendees back to the Union Station.

History of The Tacoma Method

November 3, 2026, is the 141st anniversary of the 1885 expulsion of all remaining Chinese residents of Tacoma (possibly as many as 200 people). Many Chinese had left earlier that fall because of the hostile atmosphere here in Tacoma. The Chinese Must Go campaign was not an official act of the City government, but it was openly instigated and organized by elected officials (including the mayor and members of the City Council) and other leading citizens of civic influence. Soon after the event, the expulsion became known as the Tacoma Method in a rising tide of anti-Chinese sentiment and acts of violence in the western United States.

Join us in solidarity on Saturday, October 24th as we commit ourselves to anti-racism in the City of Destiny.

For more information, visit crpftacoma.org or contact Ben Everett at info@crpftacoma.org.
